units.function: Focused unit suite for raw WebSocket upgrade socket cleanup when authenticated live-event authorization rejects, the peer closes early or the socket errors asynchronously.
units.dependencyDirection: Drives the live-events WebSocket server setup through a fake HTTP server and raw Duplex-like socket; session resolution and logger are seams, while no database/event source is used.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP upgrade request path/headers, deployment mode, asynchronous session result, raw socket writable/ended/destroyed state and warning log.
units.lifecycle: Receive upgrade; start asynchronous authorization; handle early close or error; optionally write 403; destroy socket; remove temporary listeners.
units.testAssessment: Three fast unit cases pass and specifically cover close-before-reject, EPIPE-during-auth and listener cleanup after 403. They do not validate successful sessions, tenant/path authorization, Origin/Host, token transport, event projection, replay/ordering, reconnect, rate/size/backpressure or redaction.
units.designRationale: Prevent process crashes, write-after-close errors and listener leaks in an asynchronous HTTP-upgrade rejection path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a secure, resumable tenant-scoped event stream for its Web, mobile clients and Connectors, including reliable transport cleanup under adversarial network behavior.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY for raw-socket cleanup tests. Company OS EventPort should expose authenticated tenant/principal subscriptions, allowed event families, monotonically ordered cursor/sequence, resume window and snapshot fallback, bounded payloads, backpressure/slow-consumer eviction, heartbeat/expiry and structured disconnect codes. Browser transport additionally needs explicit Origin and credential policy; every event projection must enforce organization, data-contract and responsibility visibility before publication.
units.responsibilityConflict: Transport cleanup has no direct conflict, but a live stream without proven tenant/principal and responsibility visibility filtering could expose goals, approvals, evidence or Agent activity to an unauthorized observer. These tests provide no evidence for that boundary.
evidence: git history: e93d78b46c1dc074086ff958bc1de3378701cbc7 recorded in the read ledger
units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: errors during pending auth are contained; no write occurs after close; rejection cleanup removes listeners and destroys the socket. CRITICAL evidence gap: successful authentication and company subscription authorization are entirely untested here. HIGH browser-security gap: Origin/Host/subprotocol and cookie/token behavior are untested. HIGH confidentiality gap: event-level tenant/data/responsibility projection is untested. HIGH availability gap: rate, size, replay, backpressure and slow-consumer behavior are untested.
